schema at `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:67` and validate it in
the handler at `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1272`. Accepts

through the handler so the new pipeline-creation request
carries `mode` in its payload (the `/api/v1/pipelines`
POST body — extend the `data` dict at
`orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1277` accordingly). Reject any

regex check at 1281). No-op for ISSUE-mode pipelines that

tasks.description:
Implement reassess auto-detection. When `mode == "auto"`
and the issuetype is `Epic`, query the gateway's
`POST /api/v1/jira/search` (`gateway/gateway.py:5015`) with
**two separate JQL queries** and merge the results
(architect ad-9, risk_analyst R4): query A
`parent = "<KEY>"`; query B `"Epic Link" = "<KEY>"` —
unless `resolve_hierarchy_field(project_key) == "parent"`
(TASK-1-4), in which case query B is skipped as a
tautology. Each query is dispatched independently; an
HTTP 400 from Atlassian on either query (typically
*"Field 'Epic Link' does not exist or you do not have
permission to view it"* on team-managed/Next-gen projects)
is **tolerated**: log a structured `jira_epic_search_field_missing`
warning and treat that query's result set as empty. The
merged child set (union of both queries by `key`) drives
the auto-detection decision. Non-empty merged results →
set the pipeline's effective mode to `reassess`; empty →
`fresh`. When `mode == "reassess"` and the merged set is
empty, log a warning and gracefully degrade to `fresh`
(decision-12). When `mode == "fresh"` and children exist,
log a warning and proceed with fresh (the operator asked
for it explicitly). Persist the resolved effective mode on
`Pipeline` via a new
`Pipeline.jira_effective_mode: Literal["fresh", "reassess"] | None`
field so downstream phases read it without re-detecting.
The two-query helper is exported as
`search_epic_children(epic_key, project_key) -> list[dict]`
from `orchestrator/jira_epic_detect.py` so TASK-1-12 reuses
it.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- The implementation issues TWO independent JQL queries
  (or one when the project's hierarchy field is `parent`)
  and merges results by `key`. Single-query disjunctive
  `parent = ... OR "Epic Link" = ...` is **not** used —
  it fails on team-managed projects where `"Epic Link"`
  doesn't exist (architect ad-9).
- HTTP 400 on either query alone does NOT fail the sweep:
  it is logged and the query's result set is treated as
  empty.
- `auto` resolves to `reassess` when the merged child set
  is non-empty, `fresh` when it's empty.
- `reassess` on a childless epic emits a structured warning
  and degrades to `fresh`.
- `fresh` on an epic with children emits a structured
  warning and proceeds.
- `Pipeline.jira_effective_mode` is populated and persisted.
- Submit-task with `jira_ticket` set completes within ~2 s
  on a healthy gateway (synchronous detection probe is on
  the critical path); the orchestrator emits a STATUS
  message when total submit_task latency exceeds 5 s so
  operators can tune (architect oq-6 / risk_analyst R15).
- Unit tests in `orchestrator/tests/test_jira_reassess_detection.py`
  cover: both-queries-succeed, `parent`-only-succeeds,
  `Epic Link`-only-succeeds, BOTH-400, mode-degradation
  paths, and the latency-warning emission.

tasks.description:

- `resolve_hierarchy_field` returns the mapped value for a

tasks.description:
New orchestrator-side Jira transitions client at
`orchestrator/jira_transitions.py` plus a **shared
credential loader module** at
`shared/egg_jira_credentials.py` (risk_analyst R1
single-source-of-truth, reviewer non-blocking #3 option
a). Refactor `gateway/jira_credentials.py` so its
`_load_credentials` body and the
`JiraCredentials`/`JiraCredentialsUnavailable` dataclasses
live in `shared/egg_jira_credentials.py`; the existing
gateway-side module re-exports them so existing imports
(`from gateway.jira_credentials import get_jira_credentials`)
continue to resolve. `orchestrator/jira_transitions.py`
then imports the loader from the shared module — no
orchestrator → gateway one-way coupling.

Transitions go orchestrator-direct because the gateway
permanently blocks `transitions` (per
`gateway/jira_client.py:32-40` ALLOWED_METHODS and the
path-denylist note at `jira_client.py:39-41`). Surface:
`JiraTransitionsClient.transition_to_wont_do(key: str,
comment: str) -> TransitionResult` — calls
`POST /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions` with the
`Won't Do` transition ID resolved via
`GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}/transitions` (Jira project
workflows vary, so the transition ID is looked up per
project and cached).

**Idempotency on re-run**: before dispatching the
transition, fetch `GET /rest/api/3/issue/{key}` and
compare `fields.status.name` against the target. If the
child is already in `Won't Do` (or any status whose
category matches "Done"), short-circuit and return
`TransitionResult(status="already_in_state")` — re-runs
must not 400 on "transition is invalid".

**Feature flag (risk_analyst R1 default-off)**: gate the
client behind `EGG_ENABLE_ORCH_JIRA_TRANSITIONS=true` env
var (default `false`). When disabled, the client raises
`OrchJiraTransitionsDisabled` and the caller logs +
surfaces a HITL asking the operator to enable. This
preserves the strict zero-credential default for installs
that haven't opted into the orchestrator-direct cred
surface.

Emits one structured log line per attempted transition
with fields
`{epic_key, child_key, from_status, to_status, principal=ATLASSIAN_USERNAME}`
(per feedback Q1's audit requirement). Surfaces 4xx/5xx
as `JiraTransitionFailed` so callers can record partial
state in `epic_apply.wont_do_batch[].error`.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- `shared/egg_jira_credentials.py` exists and exports
  `JiraCredentials`, `JiraCredentialsUnavailable`,
  `get_jira_credentials`,
  `get_jira_credentials_manager`,
  `parse_env_file` (re-exported through the existing
  `gateway/jira_credentials.py` for backward compat).
- `JiraTransitionsClient` reuses the shared loader — no
  duplicate cred parsing, no `from gateway...` import.
- `transition_to_wont_do` looks up the project's
  `Won't Do` transition ID dynamically and caches it.
- `transition_to_wont_do` returns
  `status="already_in_state"` when the child's current
  status is already `Won't Do`; idempotent re-runs do
  NOT issue the transition or 400 on it.
- The client is gated by
  `EGG_ENABLE_ORCH_JIRA_TRANSITIONS=true` (default
  disabled); when disabled, raises
  `OrchJiraTransitionsDisabled`.
- Audit log line is emitted in the exact shape feedback Q1
  specifies for every attempted (or skipped-as-no-op)
  transition.
- Unit tests in
  `orchestrator/tests/test_jira_transitions_client.py`
  cover happy path, already-in-state short-circuit, 403,
  404, transition-not-found (`JiraTransitionFailed`),
  cred-missing (`JiraCredentialsUnavailable`), and
  feature-flag-disabled
  (`OrchJiraTransitionsDisabled`).

tasks.description:
Add `EpicApplyArtifact` Pydantic model to
`orchestrator/models.py` (sibling of `HITLDecision` at
`models.py:277` and `PhaseExecution` at `models.py:363`).
Schema:
`{ version: int = 1,
   idempotency_seed: str,
   refine_description_sha256: str | None,
   plan_node_to_jira_key: dict[str, str],
   applied_edits: list[{kind: literal["create"|"edit"|"link"|"comment"],
                        target: str, payload: dict,
                        summary_hash: str,
                        applied_at: datetime | None,
                        status: literal["pending"|"applied"|"failed"|"skipped"],
                        error: str | None}],
   wont_do_batch: list[{child_key: str,
                        wont_do_reason: str,
                        status: literal["pending"|"applied"|"failed"|"already_in_state"],
                        error: str | None}],
   in_flight_gates: list[{child_key: str,
                          proposed_mutation: str,
                          signal_source: list[literal["jira_status"|"orchestrator_pr_url"|"remote_link"]],
                          signal_detail: dict[str, str],
                          linked_pr_url: str | None,
                          decision_id: str | None}] }`.
`version` is the schema version (forward-compat per
risk_analyst R10); `idempotency_seed` is a per-pipeline
UUID stamped at refine-apply time and passed as
Atlassian's `X-Atlassian-Idempotency-Key` on every
`createJiraIssue` so retries don't duplicate;
`refine_description_sha256` records the epic Description
the refine agent observed (architect ad-5 concurrent-edit
guard); `summary_hash` per edit lets re-runs detect "same
edit, different ts" cleanly; `wont_do_reason` per Won't-Do
entry seeds the plan-draft per-row reason that operators
scrutinise at decision-3 batch approval (risk_analyst R6).
`signal_source` becomes a **list** (decision-8 OR
semantics — multiple signals can fire at once).

Serialised to JSON and stored in
`Pipeline.phases["plan"].artifacts["epic_apply"]` — mirrors
the existing `phases["pr"].artifacts["pr_url"]` precedent
at `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py:1727`. Provide getter +
setter helpers on `Pipeline` (e.g. `get_epic_apply()` /
`set_epic_apply()`) so call sites don't manipulate the
raw dict.

Add a new MCP tool **`mcp__sdlc__update_epic_apply(payload)`**
to `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py` so the sandbox-side
`apply_epic` agent can persist artifact updates without
direct file access. Handler validates the payload against
`EpicApplyArtifact`, calls `Pipeline.set_epic_apply()`
inside the orchestrator process, and returns the
updated version + a structured 4xx on validation
failures.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- `EpicApplyArtifact` exists with the schema above
  (including `version`, `idempotency_seed`,
  `refine_description_sha256`, per-edit `summary_hash`
  and `applied_at`, per-Won't-Do `wont_do_reason`,
  `signal_source` as a **list**) and passes Pydantic
  round-trip.
- `Pipeline.get_epic_apply()` returns `None` when the
  artifact isn't set, the parsed model otherwise.
- `Pipeline.set_epic_apply()` writes JSON-encoded payload
  to `phases["plan"].artifacts["epic_apply"]`.
- The new `mcp__sdlc__update_epic_apply` MCP tool is
  registered, accepts a payload conforming to
  `EpicApplyArtifact`, rejects malformed payloads with a
  structured 400, and atomically rewrites
  `phases["plan"].artifacts["epic_apply"]`.
- Unit tests in `orchestrator/tests/test_epic_apply_artifact.py`
  cover empty round-trip, the four `applied_edits` kinds,
  the three `signal_source` enum values, version
  forward-compat, idempotency_seed round-trip, MCP-tool
  happy path, MCP-tool malformed-payload rejection.

tasks.description:
Add the refine input gatherer at
`orchestrator/jira_epic_inputs.py`. When the refine phase
starts for an epic-keyed pipeline, the gatherer assembles:
(a) the epic's own summary + description + remote links
(`getJiraIssue` at `gateway.py:4932` plus the new
`remotelinks` route from TASK-1-6); (b) every child
ticket's key/summary/status/description (JQL via
`gateway.py:5015`); (c) Confluence pages discovered per
decision-7 — remote-link URLs on the epic, URL-scrape on
the epic's description body, plus remote-links on linked
Jira issues (recursive **one** level only — a strict
depth cap to prevent runaway recursion). The gathered
context is dropped into the sandbox under
`.egg-state/agent-outputs/<id>-refine-input.json` so the
refine prompt can `Read` it. Additionally, the gatherer
computes `sha256` of the epic's current Description and
writes it into the (initially-empty)
`epic_apply.refine_description_sha256` artifact field
(TASK-1-7) via the new `mcp__sdlc__update_epic_apply`
MCP tool. The refine-apply step (TASK-1-10) re-fetches
and compares to detect concurrent-edit divergence.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- `gather_refine_inputs(pipeline)` returns a structured
  dict with the three input sections.
- Confluence link discovery is exactly one level deep
  (test with two-level chain → second-level not pulled).
- URL-scrape extracts only Confluence URLs (filter regex
  against `confluence.atlassian.net` / `<tenant>.atlassian.net/wiki`).
- Output file is written under
  `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<id>-refine-input.json` and is
  JSON-decodable.
- Unit tests in
  `orchestrator/tests/test_jira_epic_inputs.py` cover all
  three input sections, recursion depth cap, URL-scrape
  filter, and the Done-children handling (Done children
  still appear in refine input so the agent has full
  context; the exclusion is plan-prompt only per decision-4).

tasks.description:
Implement the refine apply step for the epic flow. Full
new-agent-role registration (every one of these must
land — a partial registration will fail to spawn the
agent at runtime):
1. **AgentRole enum** — add `APPLY_EPIC = "apply_epic"` to
   `shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py` (the canonical
   AgentRole source per `orchestrator/models.py:122`).
2. **AgentRoleDefinition** — add an `APPLY_EPIC_ROLE =
   AgentRoleDefinition(role=AgentRole.APPLY_EPIC,
   description=..., dependencies=..., included_tools=...,
   file_patterns=...)` entry alongside the existing
   `ARCHITECT_ROLE`, `TASK_PLANNER_ROLE`, etc. The
   `file_patterns` block declares the agent's file-write
   boundaries (the agent does not write source files —
   only `.egg-state/agent-outputs/`).
3. **Phase scheduler** — register the role in
   `get_roles_for_phase()` (same file) under both the
   `refine` and `plan` phases (gated by an
   `is_epic_pipeline` predicate so non-epic pipelines
   never spawn the role).
4. **File-restrictions** — add a corresponding row to
   `shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py` so the gateway
   accepts pushes from the role (even though the role
   does no source-tree writes, the gateway must recognise
   the role name; default-deny on an unrecognised role
   is the failure mode).
5. **Spawner branch** — add the apply-epic spawn block in
   `orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py` (alongside the
   existing concurrent-phase agent spawners). Sandbox
   env exports add `EGG_JIRA_EPIC_KEY` and
   `EGG_JIRA_HIERARCHY_FIELD` (the resolved per-project
   choice from TASK-1-4) alongside the existing
   `EGG_JIRA_TICKET` exports at
   `orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:17092` and
   `orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:19286-19289`.

Wire the role's first dispatch (refine-mode apply) to
run after the refine-phase HITL approval when
`pipeline.jira_epic_key` is set. The agent prompt lives
as a Python module-level string constant at
`orchestrator/agent_prompts/apply_epic.py`
(`APPLY_EPIC_REFINE_PROMPT`), kept as `.py` so the coder
role can author it. *Why a separate module rather than
inline in `_build_phase_prompt` at
`orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:11039`*: the existing
`_build_phase_prompt` is keyed off the four pipeline
phases (refine/plan/implement/pr), each of which is a
producer-phase prompt rendered before agent work begins;
the apply-epic agent runs AFTER a HITL approval and
consumes the approved draft as input, so its prompt has
a different lifecycle and dispatch site. Co-locating
with the existing prompt builder would conflate two
dispatch lifecycles; a separate module keeps the
existing prompt-build surface intact.

The prompt instructs the agent to:
- Read the refine draft from
  `.egg-state/drafts/<id>-analysis.md`.
- Read the epic key from `$EGG_JIRA_EPIC_KEY`.
- Call `GET /api/v1/jira/ticket/<KEY>` to fetch the
  current Description and compute `sha256`.
- Compare against
  `epic_apply.refine_description_sha256` (set by the
  refine input gatherer in TASK-1-9 when it first
  recorded the epic state). On divergence, register a
  HITL via `mcp__sdlc__register_open_question`
  ("Operator edited the epic Description after refine
  kick-off — confirm or skip overwrite?") and pause
  apply until resolved.
- On match or operator-confirm, call
  `PUT /api/v1/jira/ticket/<KEY>/edit` with the
  wholesale `Description` rewrite (decision-9).
- Persist the result via the new
  `mcp__sdlc__update_epic_apply` tool (TASK-1-7) with
  an `applied_edits[]` entry (`kind="edit"`,
  `target=<KEY>`, `summary_hash=sha256(new_body)`,
  `applied_at=<now>`, `status="applied"`).
On failure, the agent fails loudly (the orchestrator
catches and surfaces the error to the operator).
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- All FIVE registration steps land (each verified
  independently): (a) `AgentRole.APPLY_EPIC` in
  `shared/egg_contracts/agent_roles.py`; (b)
  `APPLY_EPIC_ROLE` AgentRoleDefinition in the same
  file; (c) registered in `get_roles_for_phase()` for
  refine AND plan phases (gated by epic predicate); (d)
  row in `shared/egg_restrictions/patterns.py`; (e)
  spawner branch in
  `orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py` exporting
  `EGG_JIRA_EPIC_KEY` + `EGG_JIRA_HIERARCHY_FIELD`.
- The agent prompt module
  `orchestrator/agent_prompts/apply_epic.py` exists and
  exports `APPLY_EPIC_REFINE_PROMPT` (refine mode) — the
  plan-mode constant `APPLY_EPIC_PLAN_PROMPT` is added
  by TASK-1-13.
- Concurrent-edit guard: the agent fetches the current
  Description, sha256s it, compares to
  `refine_description_sha256`, opens a divergence HITL
  on mismatch, and pauses apply until resolved.
- The orchestrator spawner spawns an `apply_epic`
  container after refine-HITL approval iff
  `pipeline.jira_epic_key` is set.
- The agent successfully edits the epic Description via
  the gateway (integration test with mocked gateway).
- Failure paths (gateway 4xx/5xx) are surfaced; the
  orchestrator marks the phase FAILED with the upstream
  error.
- Unit tests in
  `orchestrator/tests/test_apply_epic_agent_refine.py`
  cover spawn-condition, draft read, gateway call shape,
  and failure handling.

tasks.description:
Tweak the plan prompt branch at
`orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:11301` AND extend the
plan parser at `shared/egg_contracts/plan_parser.py` so
the new YAML blocks ship through to the contract. When
`pipeline.jira_epic_key` is set, the rendered prompt
instructs:
- Each plan node MUST emit a Jira-ticket-shaped
  description with the fixed structure
  `Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria /
  Out of scope / Cross-links` (feedback Q2).
- Cross-task dependencies use one of
  `{Blocks, Is blocked by, Relates to}` per edge with
  the rationale surfaced in the plan draft (feedback Q3).
- When `jira_effective_mode == "reassess"`: include the
  existing-children sweep output (TASK-1-12) and
  instruct the agent to produce a classified diff
  (`updated / closed / untouched / net-new /
  consolidated / split / in-flight`). Done children are
  **excluded** entirely (decision-4). In-flight children
  carry a `do-not-modify-without-confirmation` marker;
  net-new children that depend on an in-flight child

tasks.description:
New existing-children sweep at
`orchestrator/jira_existing_children.py`. Inputs: epic
key. Output: a list of `ExistingChild` records with
fields `{key, summary, status, description,
classification: literal["done"|"to_do"|"in_flight"],
in_flight_signals: list[{source: literal["jira_status"|
                                      "orchestrator_pr_url"|
                                      "remote_link"],
                          detail: str}]}`.

Detection:
1. Fetch children via the **`search_epic_children`** helper
   exported by `orchestrator/jira_epic_detect.py`
   (TASK-1-3) — two independent JQL queries
   (`parent = "<KEY>"` and `"Epic Link" = "<KEY>"`),
   merged by `key`, with per-query HTTP 400 tolerance.
   NOT a single-OR disjunctive (architect ad-9).
2. For each child, classify by `fields.status.name`:
   `Done` → `done`; one of `{In Progress, In Review,
   Code Review, Blocked}` → `in_flight` (signal:
   `jira_status`); else → `to_do`.
3. For non-`done` children, cross-check against the
   orchestrator's pipeline state. To avoid the O(N) scan
   of every `.egg-state/pipelines/<KEY>.json` file flagged
   by risk_analyst R3, the helper reads a single
   reverse-index file (NEW —
   `.egg-state/jira-child-pipeline-index.json` maintained
   by the orchestrator at pipeline-creation time) mapping
   `<JIRA-KEY> -> [pipeline_id, ...]`. For each
   pipeline_id, load its JSON and check
   `phases["pr"].artifacts["pr_url"]` — if set, flag
   `in_flight` (signal: `orchestrator_pr_url`,
   detail = the PR URL).
4. For non-`done` children, also fetch their
   `remotelinks` via the new gateway route (TASK-1-6).
   If any remote link's `object.url` matches
   `^https?://github\.com/.*/pull/\d+`, flag
   `in_flight` (signal: `remote_link`, detail =
   matched URL).
OR semantics (decision-8): any positive signal flips
the classification to `in_flight` and all firing signal
sources are recorded.

- All three signal sources are recorded when more than
  one fires.
- Done children correctly classify as `done` (no PR
  cross-check needed).
- With 100 historical pipelines on disk, the sweep for a
  30-child epic completes in ≤2 s wall-clock
  (integration-test bounded — risk_analyst R3
  performance budget).
- Unit tests in

  cover: status-only `in_flight`, PR-artifact-only
  `in_flight`, remote-link-only `in_flight`, multi-signal
  `in_flight`, plain `to_do`, plain `done`.

tasks.description:
Implement the plan apply step. Extend the `apply_epic`
agent (TASK-1-10) so when invoked after plan-phase HITL
approval, it reads the plan draft's `epic_apply:`
section (TASK-1-11), `consolidations:`, `splits:`, the
existing-children sweep (TASK-1-12), and the hierarchy
config (TASK-1-4), then performs the batch:
1. `createJiraIssue` for each net-new node — uses
   either `parent` or `epicLink` per
   `resolve_hierarchy_field(project_key)`.
2. `editJiraIssue` for each `edit` action target.
3. For each consolidation: `editJiraIssue` on the
   survivor + `addCommentToJiraIssue` redirect on the
   others (the Won't-Do transition is handled by
   TASK-1-14, not by the agent).
4. For each split: `editJiraIssue` on the original to
   the narrowed scope, `createJiraIssue` for the new
   nodes.
5. `createIssueLink` for each cross-task edge.
6. **In-flight gating with apply-time re-check**: before
   performing any `edit`/`Won't-Do`/`consolidate-away`
   action whose target is classified `in_flight`, the
   agent calls back to the orchestrator via the existing
   MCP server (a new `mcp__sdlc__register_in_flight_gate`
   tool registered in `orchestrator/mcp_tools.py`) to open
   a per-ticket HITL decision (TASK-1-17 implements the
   orchestrator side). The agent suspends the in-flight
   targets and applies only the non-in-flight set. The
   agent additionally **re-invokes
   `sweep_existing_children` (TASK-1-12) immediately
   before each mutation** so an in-flight transition that
   happened between plan-approval and apply is caught —
   targets that newly classify as `in_flight` at apply
   time are routed to the same HITL gate. Note v1
   trust-boundary trade-off: the agent is responsible for
   the gate dispatch (decision-11's hybrid path) —
   gateway-side enforcement is deferred to a follow-up
   (see Trust-boundary section). The apply-time re-check
   is the v1 defence-in-depth.
7. **Concurrent-edit guard** (architect ad-5): before
   calling `editJiraIssue` on the epic Description in the
   refine-mode dispatch (TASK-1-10), the agent fetches the
   current Description and computes `sha256` against
   `epic_apply.refine_description_sha256` (recorded by
   the refine apply step at TASK-1-10). On mismatch
   (operator edited the Description between refine
   kick-off and refine-apply), the agent opens a
   divergence HITL via
   `mcp__sdlc__register_open_question` and pauses apply
   until resolved. Decision-9's wholesale-rewrite
   resolution still drives the outcome, but the operator
   gets to confirm/skip the overwrite when divergence is
   detected.
After each call, the agent persists the updated
`epic_apply` artifact via a new MCP tool
`mcp__sdlc__update_epic_apply(payload)` registered in
`orchestrator/mcp_tools.py` (TASK-1-7 adds the schema +
handler) — the orchestrator-process method
`Pipeline.set_epic_apply()` is invoked server-side from
the MCP handler. Idempotent re-runs: on retry, skip any
`applied_edits[]` entry with `status == "applied"`; the
`idempotency_seed` field (TASK-1-7) seeds Atlassian
idempotency for `createJiraIssue` so a retry after a
successful create-but-failed-record does NOT create a
duplicate ticket.
tasks.acceptance_criteria:
- The agent applies a fresh-epic plan correctly:
  all `createJiraIssue` + `createIssueLink` calls
  land; no `editJiraIssue` is issued.
- The agent applies a reassess plan with mixed
  classifications correctly: net-new + edits +
  consolidations land; `Won't-Do` targets are NOT
  transitioned by the agent (left to TASK-1-14);
  in-flight mutation targets are NOT touched (a
  HITL gate is opened instead).
- The agent re-invokes `sweep_existing_children`
  immediately before each mutation; a target that
  became `in_flight` between plan approval and apply
  is routed to the HITL gate rather than mutated.
- For the refine-apply path, the agent fetches the
  current epic Description before
  `editJiraIssue` and registers a divergence HITL when
  `sha256` differs from
  `epic_apply.refine_description_sha256`.
- The `epic_apply` artifact is persisted after each
  mutation via the new
  `mcp__sdlc__update_epic_apply` MCP tool; a re-run
  with a partial artifact resumes from the first
  non-`applied` entry, and a retry of a previously
  successful `createJiraIssue` does NOT create a
  duplicate (idempotency_seed exercise).
- Hierarchy-field selection: a
  `JiraHierarchyUnmappedError` from
  `resolve_hierarchy_field` causes the agent to fail
  loudly without partial application of the affected
  project's nodes.
- Unit tests in
  `orchestrator/tests/test_apply_epic_agent_plan.py`
  cover fresh-epic, reassess-epic, in-flight gating,
  apply-time re-check (target became in_flight after
  plan approval), description-divergence HITL,
  partial-failure resume, duplicate-create-prevention

  failure path.

tasks.description:
Implement orchestrator-direct Won't-Do transitions for
non-in-flight obsolete children. After `apply_epic`
finishes the plan-apply batch and persists
`epic_apply.wont_do_batch[]` (TASK-1-13), the
orchestrator iterates the batch and calls
`JiraTransitionsClient.transition_to_wont_do(key, comment)`
(TASK-1-5) for each entry whose target is **not**
classified `in_flight` (in-flight Won't-Do mutations
have already been redirected to the per-ticket HITL
gate by TASK-1-13/TASK-1-17). The redirect comment
points at the survivor (for consolidations) or notes
"obsolete after reassess of epic <KEY>" (for plain
obsolete). Atomic-batch semantics per decision-3: the
orchestrator attempts every transition and records
successes/failures in
`epic_apply.wont_do_batch[].status` / `.error`; a
partial failure does NOT halt the remaining transitions
(operators can manually retry via re-run, which is
idempotent against the persisted artifact). The
orchestrator first checks the feature-flag
(`EGG_ENABLE_ORCH_JIRA_TRANSITIONS`) — when disabled
(default), the wont_do_batch is left in `status="pending"`
and a HITL is opened asking the operator to enable
orchestrator-direct transitions (TASK-1-5).

denylist-scope-creep invariant.

tasks.description:
Plan-gate fork (decision-6). Extend the plan-phase
HITL decision shape so the operator chooses between
`Stop-after-plan` and `Continue-to-implement`. The
decision is registered via the existing
`Pipeline.add_decision` helper (`models.py:1016`)
immediately after the plan apply step completes; the
existing plan-gate code path consumes the resolution
and either marks the pipeline `COMPLETE` (Stop) or
fans out per-child slices into the implement-phase
slice DAG (Continue). Each fanned-out child pipeline
is a separate ISSUE-mode pipeline (the orchestrator
creates one per child via the existing pipeline-creation
POST), and TASK-1-15's `Pipeline.jira_parent_epic_key`
is populated on each child pipeline at fan-out time
(the orchestrator already knows the parent epic — no
extra Jira call needed). For Stop-after-plan
pipelines, the orchestrator's status reporting and
observers (overseer monitor, babysit-pr) must accept
a documented terminal phase. Add a new
`PipelinePhase.PLAN_STOPPED` value to
`orchestrator/models.py` (or a `final_phase: str |
None` Pipeline field) so `current_phase = "plan_stopped"
+ state = COMPLETE` is the terminal-without-PR signal;
observers that today require a PR phase (e.g.
overseer-monitor's "no pr_url in phase artifacts"
alert at `orchestrator/overseer/monitor.py:1602`) are
updated to short-circuit on `plan_stopped`. The
existing slice-DAG implement loop at
`orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:17692`
(`to_contract_slices`) already supports N stacked
PRs for Continue-to-implement, so the per-child fan-out
is wiring rather than new DAG machinery.

tasks.description:

- The proposed mutation (e.g. "Edit description to: …",

- The firing signal source(s) (per decision-8).
- The linked PR URL (if any).
- The current Jira status.
The decision is stored on `epic_apply.in_flight_gates[].decision_id`.
When the operator resolves the decision, the
pipeline re-spawns the `apply_epic` agent which reads
the resolved decisions and applies only the
`Confirm`ed mutations (idempotency from TASK-1-13's
`applied_edits[]` persistence).

pr.title: Add SDLC pipeline support for Jira epics
pr.description:
Treats a Jira **epic** as the SDLC unit of work. The same
`submit_task` pipeline that runs against a regular Jira ticket
today is extended to accept an epic key: the refine output writes
to the epic's `Description`, the plan output materialises as child
Jira tickets under the epic, and a `reassess` path handles epics
that already have children (updating, consolidating, splitting,
or marking obsolete ones `Won't Do`).

Key changes:

1. **`submit_task --mode={auto,reassess,fresh}`** — new param on
   the MCP tool. Default `auto` preserves today's behaviour;
   `auto` on an epic key auto-detects reassess when children
   exist. `fresh` / `reassess` explicit overrides bypass detection
   (#1557 decision-12).
2. **Epic-vs-ticket detection** — `getJiraIssue` is called up
   front; when `fields.issuetype.name == "Epic"`, the epic-keyed
   flow runs; otherwise the existing ticket-keyed flow is used.
3. **Refine sink** — after HITL approval, a new `apply_epic`
   agent dispatches `editJiraIssue` to wholesale-rewrite the
   epic `Description` with the refined analysis (decision-9).
4. **Plan sink** — the plan prompt produces per-node Jira-ticket
   descriptions with a fixed structure (Problem statement / Scope
   / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links). After
   HITL approval, the `apply_epic` agent applies the batch:
   `createJiraIssue` for net-new nodes, `editJiraIssue` for
   updates, `editJiraIssue` + `addCommentToJiraIssue` for
   consolidations, `createJiraIssue` for splits, and
   `createIssueLink` for cross-task edges. The plan-node →
   Jira-key mapping is persisted to
   `phases["plan"].artifacts["epic_apply"]` for idempotent
   re-runs (decision-10).
5. **Reassess flow** — when an epic has children, the planner
   sees a classified diff (`done` / `to_do` / `in_flight` /
   `updated` / `consolidated` / `split` / `net-new`). The
   in-flight signal sources (Jira status, orchestrator
   `pr_url` artifact, remote-link PR URL) are OR'd together
   per decision-8; any in-flight mutation (edit / Won't-Do /
   consolidate-away) is refused by the apply step and instead
   opens a per-ticket HITL gate citing the firing signal.
   Non-in-flight obsolete children are transitioned to
   `Won't Do` atomically by the orchestrator after the
   single plan approval (decision-3).
6. **Per-project hierarchy-field config** — a new
   `~/.config/egg/jira-hierarchy.yaml` lets operators map each
   Jira project to `parent` or `epic_link` (decision-2). The
   apply step refuses unmapped projects.
7. **Orchestrator-direct Jira transitions** — `transitions`
   stays off the agent-facing gateway. A new
   `orchestrator/jira_transitions.py` client reads the same
   `~/.config/egg/secrets.env` creds (feedback Q1) and calls
   Atlassian directly for the `Won't Do` step.
8. **Plan-gate fork** — the plan-approval HITL decision offers
   `Stop-after-plan` (pipeline terminates after Jira children
   are created) vs `Continue-to-implement` (each child becomes
   its own slice in the implement slice DAG, decision-6).
9. **PR-link writeback** — when a child's implement produces a
   PR, the orchestrator writes back a comment + (when the
   gateway exposes a write) a remote link on the Jira child
   (feedback Q4).

Impact: operators can now drive epics end-to-end from
`submit_task` instead of decomposing them by hand. The existing
single-ticket pipeline is untouched. Operator setup adds the
hierarchy YAML and (for reassess) a transition-capable Atlassian
principal in `~/.config/egg/secrets.env`. Gateway audit and
transition-denylist invariants are preserved.

questions.question: **Orchestrator-direct Jira credentials configuration**: the issue notes the orchestrator needs its own Jira credentials (separate from the gateway) to apply Won't-Do transitions, since `transitions` is permanently denylisted from the agent-facing gateway. How should these credentials be provisioned and protected? Options to consider: env vars (e.g. `EGG_ORCH_JIRA_EMAIL`/`EGG_ORCH_JIRA_TOKEN`); a config file path; the existing gateway credential store (with a separate scope tag); a per-project credential map. Whichever path is chosen, please also clarify: (a) the operator-facing setup story (where they put the creds, how rotation works); (b) audit/logging expectations for transitions performed by the orchestrator.
questions.answer: Reuse the existing ~/.config/egg/secrets.env (gateway pattern). The orchestrator's transition helper reads Atlassian creds via the same resolver pattern as gateway/jira_credentials.py — checks ATLASSIAN_BASE_URL/USERNAME/API_TOKEN first, falls back to JIRA_* per-key. No new cred surface, no new file. Operator setup: add ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN (or JIRA_API_TOKEN) to secrets.env if not already present. Rotation is the same as the gateway's. Audit/logging: orchestrator emits a structured log line per transition (epic_key, child_key, from_status, to_status, principal=ATLASSIAN_USERNAME).

questions.question: **Plan-node ticket-description structure**: every plan node becomes a Jira ticket body. Should we mandate a fixed structure in the plan prompt (e.g. `Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links`) or leave the shape to the agent's judgement per node? If fixed, please describe the exact section ordering and any project-style conventions the operator wants surfaced.
questions.answer: Mandate fixed structure with sections in this order: Problem statement / Scope / Acceptance criteria / Out of scope / Cross-links. Matches the issue's 'fully-formed Jira ticket body' goal and makes downstream `submit_task <CHILD-KEY>` predictable.

questions.question: **Cross-task dependency representation in Jira**: the issue mentions `createIssueLink` (typ. `Blocks` / `Is blocked by`). Are there other link types operator-side projects use that we should support (e.g. `Relates to`, `Causes`)? Should the plan prompt allow the agent to choose the link type per edge, or always emit `Blocks` for cross-task DAG edges?
questions.answer: Agent picks per-edge from a default allowlist of `Blocks`, `Is blocked by`, `Relates to`. Plan draft shows the chosen link type and rationale per edge so operator can override before approval.

questions.question: **PR-link writeback to Jira ticket**: when a child ticket's implement phase produces a PR, should the orchestrator (or the gateway, via the agent) automatically add a remote-link / comment back to the Jira child so the operator can navigate Jira -> PR? This isn't in the issue's explicit scope but is a natural completion of the per-child-ticket-PR resolved decision.
questions.answer: Yes — remote-link via the gateway from the implement / apply agent. Adds an issue/{key}/remotelink entry pointing at the PR URL when the PR is opened. Natural completion of per-child-ticket-PRs; uses existing gateway primitives.

questions.question: **Reassess-trigger handling**: `submit_task <EPIC-KEY>` auto-detects the reassess path when the epic has children. Is there a need for an explicit `--reassess` / `--fresh` override on `submit_task` for the case where the operator wants to force one path (e.g. ignore stale children, or treat a fresh epic as a reassess of an external system)?
questions.answer: Add a single `--mode={auto,reassess,fresh}` parameter to submit_task. Default `auto` preserves today's behavior; explicit overrides bypass detection without confirmation. (This is the same answer as decision-13.)
